response: Yes, teleoncology models of care can enable the safe delivery of chemotherapy in rural towns. According to available data, it appears to be safe to administer chemotherapy in rural towns under the supervision of medical oncologists from larger centers via teleoncology, provided that rural healthcare resources and governance arrangements are adequate. Additionally, support for general practitioners through phone or videoconferencing may reduce safety concerns, making it possible to administer intensive chemotherapy regimens at standard doses to rural patients without increased morbidity or mortality.
